fields.description: The uploaded batch this row was parsed from.
fields.label: Import Batch

fields.description: The gateway's own transfer id, unique per transfer. THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY for duplicate detection across batches -- deliberately NOT the UTR, which on Project Payments is a free-text Data field with no unique constraint, no index, 226 whitespace-padded rows and a second non-stripping writer.
fields.label: Transfer Id

fields.description: The gateway's secondary numeric id, kept verbatim for support queries. Not used for matching.
fields.label: Reference Id

fields.description: When the transfer was INITIATED (the statement's Added On), full precision. Note this is not the settlement stamp; the two can straddle a date boundary.
fields.label: Added On

fields.description: The amount credited to the beneficiary. EXCLUDES service charge and tax, so it is less than the bank debit.
fields.label: Amount

fields.description: The gateway's transfer status, verbatim (SUCCESS / FAILED / PENDING / REVERSED). Non-SUCCESS rows are STAGED and then auto-skipped so the skip stays visible. A FAILED transfer still carries a bank reference and may have a successful retry elsewhere in the same file -- both would otherwise match the same payment.
fields.label: Transfer Status

fields.description: The beneficiary name as the bank holds it. This is an ACCOUNT NAME, not a vendor name -- match it against Vendors.account_name as well as Vendors.vendor_name (174 of 1,077 vendors differ). It may also be a person where the vendor is a company.
fields.label: Beneficiary Name

fields.description: The gateway's beneficiary identifier, kept verbatim. NOT a matching signal -- it is stored nowhere else in this database, so it can never resolve to anything.
fields.label: Beneficiary Id

fields.description: Beneficiary bank account, verbatim. Compare only via the normalized form -- raw values differ by leading zeros and whitespace.
fields.label: Bank Account

fields.description: Beneficiary IFSC, verbatim. Meaningful only as a pair with the account number.
fields.label: IFSC

fields.description: The transfer remark, verbatim. Carries a project name and a purpose. MUST be Text: as Data this is PG varchar(140) and Frappe THROWS CharacterLengthExceededError rather than truncating (the same trap the expense description field hit on 2026-07-28).
fields.label: Remarks

fields.description: The bank reference number the gateway reports. This is what the accountant types into a payment's UTR field by hand, which is what makes it the strong match key.
fields.label: Bank Reference No

fields.description: Gateway service charge for this transfer. Aggregated at batch level; belongs to no settlement target.
fields.label: Service Charge

fields.description: Tax on the service charge. Aggregated at batch level with the charge.
fields.label: Service Tax

fields.description: The statement's Added by value, verbatim and TRUNCATED BY THE GATEWAY to 15 characters. Retained for provenance only -- it is NOT a matching signal and does NOT set payment_by (owner ruling: payment_by is the user who finalises the row in this import).
fields.label: Added By (raw)

fields.description: bank_account with whitespace and leading zeros stripped. The comparable form -- raw string equality fails on real data (CSV 0869102000002783 vs stored 869102000002783).
fields.label: Normalized Account

fields.description: bank_reference_no with whitespace stripped. Compared against the equally-normalized Project Payments.utr -- 226 stored UTRs are whitespace-padded and would otherwise never match.
fields.label: Normalized Reference

fields.description: The vendor this row resolved to, once a human confirmed it. A bank account is NOT a unique vendor key -- one account maps to three legally distinct D.S. Ductofab companies with different GSTs -- so resolution always proposes and a person always picks.
fields.label: Resolved Vendor

fields.description: The project this row resolved to, once a human confirmed it. Suggested from the remark, never taken as decided.
fields.label: Resolved Project

fields.description: Which ledger the match run's single suggestion lives in -- one of Project Payments, Project Expenses, Non Project Expenses. Written ONLY alongside suggested_name, and only when the row is Matched with EXACTLY ONE approved candidate; blanked on every re-run that no longer finds one, so a stale pick can never survive. Derived by services/outflow_import/status.sole_suggestion. NOT a decision -- it is what the screen opens with already ticked, and a person still confirms it.
fields.label: Suggested Doctype

fields.description: The single record the match run suggests this transfer settled, addressed together with suggested_doctype. Blank means the screen pre-selects nothing: no candidate, several candidates (the screen never guesses between two real records), or a fan-out, which has no single name to hold. A plain Data field rather than a Dynamic Link on purpose -- a suggestion must survive its target being deleted without blocking the row.
fields.label: Suggested Record

fields.description: WHY the match run pre-selected suggested_name, when it was not simply the only approved candidate. Blank means the ordinary case -- exactly one record was found (services/outflow_import/status.sole_suggestion) -- so blank is by far the common value and carries no doubt. A non-blank value is one of the Option B rule ids owned by services/outflow_import/disambiguate: project-in-remark, nearest-amount, or interchangeable. Deliberately Data and NOT Select: a Select that later narrows leaves stored values Frappe will not rewrite, which is exactly what the Unmatched->Mismatched merge needed a patch for. disambiguate.RULE_LABELS is the authority on what a value means. Cleared on every re-run alongside the suggestion pair, so a stale reason can never outlive the pick it explains.
fields.label: Suggestion Rule

fields.description: Checked when this row's suggested record was chosen by the machine rather than by a person. It is exactly 'suggested_name is set' -- a human never writes a suggestion -- and it is STORED rather than derived so Desk list views, the report builder and permissions can filter on it, which they cannot do with an expression. The same reason Outflow Import Batch carries denormalised counters. SAFETY RULE: it is written in the same frappe.db.set_value as suggested_doctype/suggested_name at every write site and never on its own, so it cannot drift from the pair it describes.
fields.label: Auto Matched

fields.description: HOW the counterpart was FOUND -- the tier of the matching ladder that produced it: 'reference' (the bank reference equals a stored UTR), 'account+IFSC' (the transfer went to a vendor's bank account and the amounts agree within Re 1), or 'project in remark' (the amounts agree within Rs 5 and the remark names the record's project). Owned by services/outflow_import/matcher.py, whose TIER_* constants are the vocabulary. This is a DIFFERENT question from suggestion_rule, which says how ONE record was chosen from what was found. Blank whenever there is no suggestion; all three provenance fields describe the pre-selection and are cleared together with it.
fields.label: Match Basis

fields.description: The row's outcome. Pending match run = staged, nothing looked up yet. Matched = at least one APPROVED record was found at this amount; confirm it to settle. Mismatched = this transfer did not line up and needs a person: EITHER the match ran and found nothing settleable (new spend, or a payment still awaiting approval) OR the bank amount disagrees with a record already recorded as Paid. Both causes are stated in outcome_note; they were separate statuses until 2026-08-10, when Unmatched was merged in because they are one job to the reviewer. Settled = we wrote, the record is now Paid. Skipped = nothing to do, and skip_reason says which nothing. Error = the write was attempted and rolled back. DERIVED ONLY by services/outflow_import/status.py.
fields.label: Row Status
fields.options:
Pending match run
Matched
Mismatched
Settled
Skipped
Error

fields.description: Why this row was skipped. REQUIRED for a manual skip (owner ruling); an automatic skip -- duplicate transfer_id, or a non-SUCCESS transfer -- carries a system-generated reason instead, because making someone retype 'duplicate' forty times is theatre.
fields.label: Skip Reason

fields.description: Human-readable detail behind a non-terminal or exception outcome -- the amount delta and its implied rate, which payment the reference disagrees with, or the target's actual status. This is the reported finding; the feature never repairs what it reports.
fields.label: Outcome Note

fields.description: When the row left Pending.
fields.label: Decided At

fields.description: Who decided this row (frappe.session.user). Data, not Link, per the house convention for actor fields.
fields.label: Decided By

fields.description: The same verdict as Outflow Row Match.settlement_origin, DENORMALISED onto the row so the review screen can filter and count on it without joining the match table -- the same reason auto_matched is stored rather than derived, and the same reason Outflow Import Batch carries counters. Blank until the row is settled. SAFETY RULE: written in the same frappe.db.set_value as row_status/decided_at/decided_by at the one settlement site, never on its own, so it cannot drift from the match record it mirrors. DISTINCT FROM auto_matched, which means only 'a suggestion existed' and says nothing about whether a person accepted it.
fields.label: Settlement Origin
fields.options:
Suggestion accepted
Suggestion overridden
No suggestion

fields.label: Source
fields.description: Denormalised from the batch so the master table can filter by it without a join. Cashfree or Cashbook.

fields.label: Suggested Expense Type
fields.description: Cashbook only. The expense type the plan chose from this row's remark, stored so the background job writes exactly what the preview showed rather than deciding again.
